items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He went with uh next thing we knew he was recording with Chubby Jackson, a tune called “Father Knickerbocker.”

ctx.x: We were brothers. We met at uh Teddy Charles, Teddy Cohen his name was. He was from Springfield, Massachusetts and he played drums up there and not a very good drummer. But he was the first guy to leave Springfield and come to New York. And he went with uh next thing we knew he was recording with Chubby Jackson, a tune called “Father Knickerbocker.” He played vibes and played the vibe solo on it and he became very well known, he still lives, he’s still around, but he used to have jam sessions at his loft on 50th…

was early ‘50s, and I climbed up the stairs and I heard the introduction to “Robin’s Nest” and I said, “Hey, I know that,” and I sat down. And Teddy knew that I was from Springfield and so he was kind. He said, “Hey, you want to play?” and I said and I said no. I just want to check it out, see what’s going on. I listened to everybody playing and started to feel a little more confident, you know, maybe I’ll play a little. So I started to take my horn out and then I heard this alto player.
